strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Existing headless.run.drive can now record and replay a bounded product stop-or-continue decision from current accepted-completion and product gate evidence.
Extends the completion state machine beyond Completed and AcceptedComplete to a finite product-level decision owned by the runtime.
Rust requires explicit decision authorization plus matching accepted-completion, terminal-completion, completion-closure, and product-evidence fingerprints before committing a decision.
Persists only bounded decision evidence in the ledger so replay does not require raw ledger, charter, manifest, prompt, provider, or file content.
Returns concise product_completion_decision status and next action metadata for headless callers without adding an inspection or dashboard wrapper.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances headless_autonomous_development with supporting agent_loop, runtime_permission_enforcement, context_management, and progress_visualization.
answers.new_capability: Existing headless.run.drive can derive, record, return, and replay a bounded product_completion_decision with product_complete, continue_development, or blocked_by_product_evidence status.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: M51.2 exposes accepted_completion, but the caller still had to decide outside Rust whether accepted completion means product completion, continued development, or insufficient evidence.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: Autonomous scheduled callers would keep making product stop-or-continue decisions from external review memory rather than a durable runtime fact.
answers.non_duplicative: Distinct from M51.1 acceptance creation, PR #241 acceptance replay hardening, and M51.2 accepted-completion routing because this consumes the accepted boundary for product-level stop authority.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. This extends the existing headless.run.drive request and result shape with optional decision authorization and bounded decision metadata.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The decision is persisted runtime execution evidence and next-action metadata, not a report, history, readiness, verdict, inspection, dashboard, or summary wrapper.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: Rust validates explicit authorization and expected fingerprints, derives the product stop-or-continue status from bounded product gate metadata, appends one product-decision ledger event, and replays it duplicate-free.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: Headless callers receive a finite Rust-owned stop, continue, or repair-evidence decision instead of interpreting raw ledgers, manifests, CI, or review notes.
answers.milestone_progress: This is the final planned M51 completion-state transition before phase-complete assessment and milestone closeout.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: M51.3 updates current and archived phase-value manifests for a runtime-owned product completion stop decision. Review must confirm guard enforcement is not weakened and the diff implements real headless.run.drive decision behavior rather than a Product DoD wrapper.

exit_criteria: headless.run.drive can record bounded product_completion_decision metadata after current accepted_completion and completion finalization evidence are present
successful decision recording requires explicit product decision authorization and expected accepted-completion, terminal-completion, completion-closure, and product-evidence fingerprints
runtime derives product_complete, continue_development, or blocked_by_product_evidence instead of exposing raw product evidence to the caller

replay of the same drive and decision returns identical decision fingerprint and does not duplicate TaskRunning, TaskCompletionAccepted, HeadlessRunSessionDriveCompleted, HeadlessRunCompletionFinalized, or HeadlessRunProductCompletionDecisionRecorded evidence
invalid, incomplete, wrapper-only, stale, missing, or malformed product evidence cannot produce a false product_complete decision
the implementation adds no new JSON-RPC method and no report/readiness/history/verdict/inspection/dashboard wrapper

RPC and ledger metadata exclude raw prompts, provider responses, final responses, file content, raw Product Charter or manifest text, diagnostics, stdout/stderr, command strings, environment values, raw request bodies, raw ledger payloads, absolute paths, canonical paths, and secrets
behavior_evidence: Rust behavior test headless_run_drive_records_product_completion_decision_and_replays validates authorized product decision recording through existing headless.run.drive, bounded continue_development output, replay stability, and single product-decision ledger evidence.

Rust behavior test headless_run_drive_blocks_invalid_product_completion_evidence validates insufficient product evidence is represented as blocked_by_product_evidence with repair_product_completion_evidence next action rather than false product_complete.
Existing M51.2 Rust tests continue to validate accepted_completion routing, unaccepted non-routing, and malformed accepted-completion denial before session mutation.
VSIX runtimeClient protocol tests validate product_completion_decision request/result metadata, malformed fingerprints, invalid status or next action, and raw product evidence field rejection.

accepted_capability: Existing headless.run.drive records and replays runtime-owned product completion stop-or-continue decisions from accepted completion and bounded product gate evidence
safety_boundary: product_completion_decision is derived only after current accepted_completion route evidence and completion finalization are present
decision recording requires explicit authorization and matching accepted-completion, terminal-completion, completion-closure, and product-evidence fingerprints
invalid or insufficient product evidence produces blocked_by_product_evidence or request denial instead of product_complete
decision metadata contains only bounded ids, status strings, category names, counts, booleans, next action, and SHA-256 fingerprints
VSIX validates transport shape only; Rust owns product stop-or-continue policy
non_goals: No report, digest, history, readiness, verdict, inspection, preview, dashboard, or summary-only wrapper
No automatic product completion without explicit authorization
No provider execution, tool execution, verifier retry, patch apply, workspace mutation, shell, git, network, or service expansion
No raw Product Charter or manifest text in ledger or RPC metadata
No milestone closeout in this implementation PR
rejected_alternatives: Adding a Product DoD report RPC was rejected because headless.run.drive already owns the runtime completion boundary.
Caller-side product stop interpretation was rejected because M51 requires Rust-owned finite completion decisions.
Treating insufficient product evidence as product_complete was rejected in favor of blocked_by_product_evidence fail-closed behavior.
Broad runtime modularization was deferred so this phase remains one bounded decision slice.
technical_debt: crates/brownie-runtime/src/lib.rs remains large and should be split only in a cohesive future refactor.
M50.1 journey admission atomicity remains separate non-blocking technical debt.
Future milestone closeout should decide whether product-completion evidence should be generated from a richer internal Product Charter model rather than caller-provided bounded fingerprints.
next_capability_rationale: If this phase is accepted, M51 should proceed to phase-complete assessment and milestone closeout rather than another completion wrapper phase.
